BEFORE AND AFTER: a 13 kWh battery instead of 10 kWh. Everything was re-run through the whole model.
- Recommendation: "Solar first" before; "Solar first" after.
- Battery size assessed: 10 kWh before; 13 kWh after.
- Battery payback: 37.2 years before; 42.9 years after.
- Annual saving: $237 before; $237 after.
- Net outlay, the installed price less the rebate: $8,806 before; $10,173 after.
- kWh the battery moves in a year: 1,574 kWh before; 1,574 kWh after.
- What the battery charged with in a year: 1,749 kWh, 0% solar surplus and 100% grid import before; 1,749 kWh, 0% solar surplus and 100% grid import after.
- Crossover, the first year the position is no longer negative: year 38 before; year 43 after.
- Warranty: the payback is outside its 10 years by 27.2 years before; the payback is outside its 10 years by 32.9 years after.
- Expected years in the home: not given, so not tested before; not given, so not tested after.

THE HOUSEHOLD ASKS
What about a 13 kWh battery?

Answer the question from this comparison, briefly: at most four sentences and under 100 words, giving the battery payback before and after the change, both exactly as written.
reply: Moving to a 13 kWh battery leaves the recommendation at "Solar first." The battery payback lengthens from 37.2 years to 42.9 years, because the annual saving stays at $237 while the net outlay rises from $8,806 to $10,173. The battery still moves 1,574 kWh a year, all charged from grid import with 0% solar surplus, so the extra capacity adds cost without adding saving. The payback also sits further outside the 10-year warranty, by 32.9 years instead of 27.2 years.
